claims.answer: Jcode provides a terminal UI and product CLI on macOS, Linux and Windows. jcode run is noninteractive, serve starts a persistent daemon and connect attaches clients. The /mobile command moves a session and its swarm to Jcode Cloud and requests a phone-app push; an existing cloud session only requests the notification. Phone operating-system availability is not specified here.

evidence.title: Jcode: Install; First run
evidence.finding: Jcode provides a terminal UI and product CLI on macOS, Linux and Windows. jcode run is noninteractive, serve starts a persistent daemon and connect attaches clients.

evidence.title: Jcode: Download
evidence.finding: Jcode Desktop has a universal macOS DMG requiring macOS 13 or newer, Linux x86_64 packages with ARM64 when available, and a portable Windows 10/11 ZIP. Linux packages are not repository-signed and the Windows app is not code-signed. The page does not label the desktop app beta.

evidence.title: Jcode: Mobile continuation
evidence.finding: The /mobile command moves a session and its swarm to Jcode Cloud and requests a phone-app push; an existing cloud session only requests the notification. Phone operating-system availability is not specified here.

evidence.title: Jcode: Providers and login; Any compatible endpoint
evidence.locator: Providers and login; Any compatible endpoint
evidence.finding: Jcode is its own coding harness with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Copilot and Azure provider logins, local Ollama/LM Studio and named OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Model-provider access does not establish running Claude Code or Codex CLI as its harness.

evidence.title: Jcode: Providers and login; Headless logins
evidence.finding: Jcode supports subscription OAuth and direct API providers, Claude subscription login and OpenAI/ChatGPT/Codex login, plus local model servers. /account switches provider accounts.

evidence.title: Jcode: First run; Remote use
evidence.finding: Install the binary, run jcode in the project folder and choose a provider login. Remote Unix hosts can run a persistent daemon reached through SSH socket forwarding.

evidence.title: Jcode: TypeScript SDK
evidence.finding: The TypeScript SDK launches a private Jcode process or attaches through api-bridge to a local or forwarded remote daemon, with session and streaming operations.

evidence.title: Jcode: MCP servers; Skills
evidence.finding: Jcode loads global and project MCP configuration and imports Claude Code/Codex MCP servers. Only stdio MCP servers are supported; HTTP/SSE entries are skipped. Markdown skills can load on relevance or explicit invocation.

evidence.title: Jcode: jcode desktop; Download
evidence.finding: The desktop app bundles the Jcode runtime and renders native diffs, Mermaid, images and tool cards. Framework internals and cross-platform parity were not source-inspected.

evidence.title: Jcode: First run
evidence.finding: Users start an interactive project session or submit a noninteractive prompt through jcode run. External-tracker intake was not established.

evidence.title: Jcode: Todo planning hierarchy
evidence.finding: Plans consist of phases, lanes and items with names, descriptions, lifecycle status, priority and confidence. Updates target names; generated internal IDs survive plan replacement when names stay the same.

evidence.title: Jcode: Todo planning hierarchy; Completely blocked
evidence.finding: Phases are ordered, lanes can run in parallel and items run in lane order. A lane can name earlier prerequisite tasks; cancelled/deleted prerequisites do not satisfy it. Completely blocked is a condition with a reason, separate from lifecycle state.

evidence.title: Jcode: First run; Other files; Skills
evidence.finding: Repository and global AGENTS.md load into the corresponding scope. Jcode also stores memory and skills, with explicit /memory and /skills controls. Memory correctness has not been tested.

evidence.title: Jcode: Swarm
evidence.finding: When one agent edits a file another has read, the server notifies the reader, which can inspect the diff. This does not prove automatic conflict-free integration.

evidence.title: Jcode: Todo planning hierarchy
evidence.finding: Native saved todo items have stable internal IDs, names, descriptions, priority, confidence, states and phase/lane membership. They are separate items inside a session plan, not a cross-project issue backlog.

evidence.title: Jcode: Coordinator; Agents
evidence.finding: The coordinator owns the shared versioned plan and can propose, approve, assign and control tasks. Workers receive an assigned todo lane rendered before work starts. Other workers cannot freely mutate the shared plan.

evidence.title: Jcode: Swarm
evidence.finding: Multiple agents can work concurrently in the same repository; the server manages messaging, completion status and file-change notifications. Actual concurrency and performance benchmarks were not rerun.

evidence.title: Jcode: Root-only spawning; Coordinator
evidence.finding: Only root sessions spawn swarm workers. The root coordinator assigns shared-plan tasks and controls that plan through a single coordinator slot.

evidence.title: Jcode: Swarm
evidence.finding: Jcode agents can autonomously spawn a swarm, making the original agent coordinator. Server-managed messages support direct, repository-wide and server-wide communication and completion status.

evidence.title: Jcode: Status; Key design decisions
evidence.finding: Ambient mode is implemented but disabled by default. It runs one proactive background agent, self-schedules wakeups and prioritizes interactive sessions; later design ideas in the document are not all shipped.

evidence.title: Jcode: Keybindings; Slash commands
evidence.finding: Enter interleaves a message with the working agent and Shift+Enter queues it. Commands can resume, fork, compact or rewind sessions.

evidence.title: Jcode: Every session on one spatial canvas
evidence.locator: Every session on one spatial canvas
evidence.finding: Desktop offers a spatial session canvas and zoomed-out overview with task and orchestration views. No six-task navigation fixture or measured effort was run.

evidence.title: Jcode: First run; Configure
evidence.finding: Users start quick prompts, headless requests or swarm sessions, with provider/model/effort and feature configuration.

evidence.title: Jcode: Remote use
evidence.finding: The daemon owns sessions, tools and provider calls. It can run locally or on a user SSH server, where it continues after disconnect; a local client can forward the remote Unix socket.

evidence.title: Jcode: Cloud session CLI
evidence.finding: Detached cloud turns run on the session recorded cloud host and reject a second active owner. /mobile migrates session and swarm to the managed Jcode Cloud host.

evidence.title: Jcode: Swarm Architecture; Worktree Manager
evidence.finding: Swarm coordination supports optional Git worktrees and worktree manager roles for separate code work and later integration. These are checkout boundaries, not hostile-code sandboxes.

evidence.title: Jcode: Uninstall; Remote use
evidence.finding: Normal uninstall retains config, authentication, memory and sessions unless purge is requested. A remote daemon keeps working after disconnection and --resume reopens its saved session.

evidence.title: Jcode: Cloud environment requirements
evidence.finding: Cloud handoff does not make machines identical. Metadata-only environment requests transfer scoped project files or allowlisted credentials; local callbacks have a limited lifetime and disconnect revokes future access. Copied resources remain until removed or rotated.

evidence.title: Jcode: Cloud session CLI
evidence.finding: cloud wait exits unsuccessfully on timeout without cancelling the remote turn. Failed inspection and remote-turn failure remain errors; an active owner blocks a detached turn.

evidence.title: Jcode: Live worker status in todo lanes
evidence.locator: Live worker status in todo lanes
evidence.finding: Todo lanes show worker activity, observed tokens, throughput, connection, elapsed time and tool intent. Missing telemetry is not inferred from context size. Waiting/stopped workers show available reasons.

evidence.title: Jcode: Slash commands; Provider usage
evidence.finding: The /usage and /info commands show provider limits, session information and tokens. Token and quota visibility is not proof of per-task invoiced spend.

evidence.title: Jcode: Key design decisions
evidence.finding: Ambient mode admits only one ambient instance and gives interactive sessions priority. Its later design/resource-policy examples are not all implemented; no safe load test was performed.

evidence.title: Jcode: Temporary callback; Credential allowlist
evidence.finding: Temporary local environment access is scoped to the handoff lease, defaults to twenty-four hours and ends on disconnect/session switch. The credential allowlist excludes arbitrary home files and SSH private keys. This is not a verified general command-approval system.

evidence.title: Jcode: Todo planning hierarchy
evidence.finding: Plan item identity is preserved through matching-name replacement and explicit rename. Transcript/log integrity and multi-user attribution were not tested.

evidence.title: Jcode: Diffs, rendered
evidence.finding: Jcode Desktop renders file diffs, Mermaid diagrams, inline images and compact tool calls beside live agent sessions. No guided human review measurement was run.

evidence.title: Jcode: Side by side, all live
evidence.finding: The desktop client renders diffs, Mermaid diagrams, inline images and tool cards beside agent conversations. Persistent revision-bound cross-task artifact retrieval remains unverified.

evidence.title: Jcode: Hill-climbable measurements
evidence.finding: Todo assessments track feedback-loop coverage, measurable outcomes and evidence for stopping. This is not proof of mandatory CI or independent passing review.

evidence.title: Jcode: Slash commands
evidence.finding: /commit makes logical commits, /commit-push can push them and /diff changes diff rendering. No product-owned PR creation flow was established.

evidence.title: Jcode: Slash commands
evidence.finding: The /rewind command rewinds a conversation. It is not evidence of repository rollback or production deployment rollback.

evidence.title: Jcode: MIT License
evidence.finding: Jcode source is MIT licensed at the pinned revision, including a free-of-charge permission grant. Optional hosted inference/cloud services have separate commercial scope.

evidence.title: Jcode: From source; Remote use
evidence.finding: The Jcode daemon, TUI and tools can run on a user-controlled machine or SSH host, with direct model credentials or local servers. Optional Jcode Cloud is not required for local use.

evidence.title: Jcode: Ordinary telemetry; How to Opt Out
evidence.locator: Ordinary telemetry; How to Opt Out
evidence.finding: Default usage telemetry may include provider OAuth email, installation ID and numeric/categorical usage. Full transcript sharing is separately opt-in. jcode telemetry disable, JCODE_NO_TELEMETRY=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or a no_telemetry file disables telemetry.

evidence.title: Jcode: Token plans; Billing details
evidence.finding: Optional hosted plans start at USD 10 monthly with USD 20 inference credit and fifty Jcode Cloud machine hours. Extra inference defaults to a zero-dollar cap; paid overage uses provider API prices after raising the cap. Remote Rust builds start at the USD 20 plan. This is separate from free MIT local software.

evidence.title: Jcode: Preview release
evidence.finding: v1.0.0-preview.199, published November 6, is an opt-in v1 pre-release of experimental binaries; the release notes direct production use to the stable channel. Open issue topics include syntax highlighting, ACP cancellation and compaction refusals, without reproduced universal findings.

evidence.title: Jcode: MIT License
evidence.finding: The application can be downloaded, used and self-hosted as free MIT software. Optional token/cloud plans and Rust-build trials have separate prices and trial conditions.

evidence.title: Jcode: Billing details
evidence.finding: The hosted plans disclose recurring USD charges, inference credit, cloud hours, API-price overage and separate build-overage limits. Local application use and model subscriptions remain separate cost routes.

evidence.title: Jcode Antigravity support at v0.99.1
evidence.finding: Jcode v0.99.1 implements Antigravity as a Google Cloud Code model-provider transport using an HTTP client and model catalog. This does not establish a separate Antigravity coding-agent session.
